title: Harden a log line parser against messy input
prompt: You are working in the current directory. There is a file `logparse.py` containing a function `parse_log(lines)` that parses a list of log line strings, each expected to look like `TIMESTAMP LEVEL MESSAGE` (fields separated by single spaces, e.g. `2024-01-01T10:00:00 INFO Server started`), into a list of dicts with keys `timestamp`, `level`, and `message`. It currently works correctly on well-formed input, but must be hardened to also handle messy real-world input without crashing. Specifically, update `parse_log` in `logparse.py` so that: (1) empty lines and lines containing only whitespace are skipped (not included in the output, no error); (2) a malformed line that does not have at least three space-separated fields (timestamp, level, and at least one word of message) is skipped (not included, no error) rather than raising an exception; (3) the LEVEL field is normalized to uppercase in the output regardless of its case in the input (e.g. `info` or `Info` becomes `INFO`); (4) a line whose (uppercased) LEVEL is not one of `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR` is skipped (not included, no error); (5) the MESSAGE field is everything after the timestamp and level (split on the first two spaces only), with its original internal spacing preserved exactly as written, not further split or stripped of internal extra spaces (only a trailing newline, if present, should be removed). The function must never raise an exception due to malformed input; it should just skip the offending line. Do not change the function's name or signature.
